instrument: City Council motion adopting a one-year moratorium and study on data centers
term: Up to 12 months, with option to renew for an additional year
notes: Council held first public hearing Aug 3, 2026 (tabled to address language), then passed the one-year moratorium with overwhelming support at its Sept 21, 2026 meeting. Pauses consideration/construction of new data centers for up to 12 months while the city studies localized impacts and how other communities regulate them; renewable for one more year.

instrument: Trustees resolution imposing a 12-month moratorium on accepting/processing zoning permits for data centers
notes: Approved at the Sept 8, 2026 trustee meeting; reported in a Sept roundup article. Township currently has no zoning rules for data centers; pause meant to give time to study other communities' regulations. Trustees separately adopted a 12-month moratorium on horizontal directional drilling / trenchless utility installations same meeting (not a data-center action).

instrument: Resolution 2026-41, Data Center and Battery Energy Storage System Development Moratorium
term: Up to 12 months from date of resolution (through approx. 2027-05-26); Board of Supervisors reserves right to extend by separate action
notes: Confirmed from the official County Board of Supervisors minutes (May 26, 2026 meeting, included in the June 23 agenda packet). Motion by Thayse, seconded by Shaw; carried by voice vote. Applies to unincorporated areas of Door County. No known data center project in the county at time of passage per Supervisor Thayse's remarks.

instrument: Board of Commissioners 60-day moratorium on accepting data center permit applications
term: 60 days (from approx. Aug 25 to approx. Oct 24, 2026)
notes: Applies only to unincorporated parts of the county. County had earlier discussed drafting a data center ordinance; officials said no projects were approved/planned and no NDAs signed as of early August 2026. Moratorium adopted so county could set permanent guidelines.

instrument: Initial: Commission-adopted temporary halt on new data center projects (moratorium, extended twice); later replaced by a permanent Data Center Ordinance
term: Moratorium ran until ordinance adopted; extended 60 days on 2026-07-21 (through mid-Sept); replaced entirely by the 21-page permanent Data Center Ordinance passed 6-5 on 2026-09-15
notes: Consolidated city-county government. Commission unanimously froze new data center projects on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 pending a permanent ordinance; extended 60 days on July 21, 2026 (after a failed 90-day substitute motion) with three added public hearings. On Sept 15, 2026 the Commission approved a comprehensive 21-page zoning/development ordinance for data centers by a 6-5 vote, which establishes siting/operational standards going forward and effectively supersedes the pause. Moratorium did not apply to the QTS campus already under construction or the Hayne's Station-area project.

instrument: County Council moratorium pausing acceptance of new data center permits, following denial of a rezoning ordinance for a proposed data center (Project Altair)
term: At least 12 months (formally confirmed as a 12-month moratorium on 2026-07-15); council retains ability to extend
notes: Council unanimously denied (on 3rd reading) an ordinance that would have allowed a developer to buy land in the Mid-Carolina Commerce Park (Prosperity) for a data center, then placed a moratorium pausing new data-center permits for at least 12 months (June 3, 2026). Council formally/unanimously confirmed the 12-month moratorium at its July 15, 2026 meeting (reported July 16).

instrument: County Board resolution - 12-month data center moratorium in unzoned areas of the county
notes: Board unanimously approved a 12-month moratorium covering the county's unzoned areas; a $2 billion data center proposal that prompted the vote reportedly went quiet/collapsed afterward per Wisconsin Watch reporting. Exact adoption date is approximate (news coverage places the vote at the county board's mid-June meeting, ~June 16, 2026, per a June 24 opinion column describing it as having passed 'last week'); could not independently confirm from a primary board-minutes document, hence moderate confidence. Note this is separate from the Town of Cassville's own (town-level) moratorium in the same county (see B17).

instrument: County Commissioners resolution - 12-month data center moratorium (construction, permits, special use conditions)
term: 12 months; remains in effect unless regulations are adopted sooner
notes: Passed unanimously (two commissioners absent) on Tuesday, June 30, 2026, a week after commissioners first discussed the idea. Gives the county time to develop regulations via planning board before the pause ends. Other nearby Nebraska counties (Otoe, Gage) adopted similar moratoriums around the same time.

instrument: City Council resolution - one-year moratorium on data centers
notes: Council held first reading July 16, 2026, then approved the one-year moratorium at its first meeting of August (Aug 7, 2026). No data center project pending at time of passage; gives council time to define 'hyper/mega' data centers and set zoning regulations.

instrument: City Council resolution - six-month moratorium on 'high utility user' applications (covers data centers, AI facilities, hydrogen production, and cryptocurrency mining)
notes: Council adopted the moratorium 5-0, per the Chisago County Press's July 31, 2026 report on the council's prior-week meeting (i.e., approx. July 28, 2026 meeting date; exact date not stated). Defines 'high utility users' as sites using 50,000+ gallons of water/day or 25-50 MW. Earlier (July 19) coverage described the measure as still 'planned.'

jurisdiction: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians (tribal and trust lands)
instrument: EBCI Tribal Council (Dinilawigi) Ordinance No. 158 (2026) - indefinite moratorium on data centers
notes: Passed 11-0 (one representative absent) on Thursday, May 7, 2026, following an April introduction/tabling and community organizing (dinner/info session April 25) led in part by Indigenous Environmental Network organizer Missy Crowe. Council clarified tribal data-storage facilities are not covered. Framed by the tribe as a 'moratorium' despite its indefinite duration, following passage of a tribal rights-of-nature resolution earlier in 2026.

instrument: Township Board resolution imposing a temporary 12-month moratorium on power generating facilities (broader than data centers)
term: 12 months or until a regulatory ordinance is enacted, whichever comes first
notes: Two separate instruments found. (1) Dec 8, 2025: Board placed a 180-day moratorium specifically on approval of data centers while directing the planning commission to study zoning - this would have expired around June 2026 and matches the 'data_center' sector, but is now expired/superseded by (2). (2) June 12, 2026 special meeting: Board passed a broader 12-month moratorium on 'power generating facilities' (establishment/permitting/construction) after Consumers Energy took an option on 120 acres for a possible 1.4-gigawatt natural gas plant; this is the 'general' sector instrument matching the packet's sector hint, and remains active.

instrument: Board of Supervisors Resolution #2026-76, Moratorium on Data Centers
notes: Read directly from the signed resolution text (dated June 16, 2026) and confirmed by news coverage: passed unanimously after a motion to table failed 3-2. Covers 'large' and 'small' scale data centers and other 'high-density facilities' in the unincorporated county, motivated by a proposed bitcoin mining operation (Octopus Investments) and a solar/data-center project (GoSolar). Board Chair Knisley suggested the eventual ordinance may be an addendum to the county's existing 2024-25 solar/wind/battery-storage ordinance.

instrument: none_found
notes: No news coverage, city document, or ordinance found indicating Rittman, Ohio has adopted or proposed a data center moratorium. Queries used: 'Rittman Ohio data center moratorium'; 'Rittman Ohio city council data center ordinance'; 'Rittman village council moratorium data center Wayne County Ohio'; '"Rittman" data center pause Ohio'; 'cityofrittman data center moratorium'; 'Rittman Ohio city council agenda data center 2026'. Statewide roundups (e.g., Ohio Capital Journal's Sept 18, 2026 list of 138 Ohio jurisdictions with active moratoriums) were not opened for a jurisdiction list per the independent-verification rules, and no Rittman-specific primary source turned up. Possible the packet intends a different/similarly-named jurisdiction, or this is a true negative.

instrument: Proposed City Council ordinance (introduced by Councilwoman Rohli Booker) - 365-day moratorium blocking approval of new data center projects
term: Proposed as one year (365 days) if adopted
notes: Introduced Sept 9, 2026 by Councilwoman Booker; would not affect the existing Google data center project already underway in southeast Fort Wayne. Council took up amendments Sept 22-23, 2026 but delayed final vote to Oct 13, 2026, so as of 2026-09-23 the moratorium has not been adopted.

instrument: City Council resolution - one-year moratorium on establishing/permitting/constructing data centers
notes: Adopted Monday, March 9, 2026 in response to a proposed 100 MW Raeden/Cal Realty data center at the former McLouth Steel site. Developers Raeden and Cal Realty sued the city in federal court on Aug 17, 2026, alleging the moratorium unlawfully targets their already-submitted application; as of the reporting available (through late August/September 2026) the moratorium remained in force and the lawsuit was pending, so status is active rather than rescinded.

instrument: Town ordinance (adopted by electors at town meeting, 44-0) banning/prohibiting data centers, plus related zoning-authority assumption
notes: At an April 16, 2026 town meeting, electors voted 44-0 to authorize town supervisors to exercise zoning authority and to adopt an ordinance prohibiting data centers in the town for up to two years, plus restricting other land-use changes without town board approval. Passed in response to a rumored ~500-acre, $1B+ data center proposal in the Driftless Area; town's attorney said the county cannot preempt the town's zoning authority in this case.

instrument: Trustees-adopted temporary moratorium on data centers
term: Not specified in sources found (other Wood County townships in the same wave adopted one-year moratoriums, but Freedom Township's specific term/expiration was not confirmed)
notes: Per BG Independent News (March 13, 2026 article, citing township fiscal officer Julie Getz), Freedom Township (surrounding Pemberville, Wood County) 'adopted a moratorium in January' 2026 to allow trustees time to research data center impacts and gather resident input; among the earliest of 7 Wood County townships to do so as of March 2026 (driven by concern over the nearby ~$800M Meta data center in Middleton Township). Could not find a primary township resolution document or exact date/term; moderate confidence only.

instrument: County Commission resolution - two-year moratorium on data centers, cryptocurrency mining facilities, and large battery storage facilities
notes: Passed unanimously at the Monday, June 15, 2026 Commission meeting (motion by Commissioner McNabb, seconded by Commissioner Allen), rejecting competing zoning-code amendments that would have allowed these uses in industrial zones with an approval process. County Law Director and Mayor said a permanent ban was not believed legally viable but a moratorium was. No applications were pending for any of the three facility types at time of passage.

instrument: Proposed City Council ordinance (introduced by Councilwoman Donyale Hall) - 18-month pause on acceptance/processing/review/approval/permitting of new data centers
term: Proposed as up to 18 months if adopted
notes: Proposal first raised by Councilwoman Hall on Aug 11, 2026; the Council's Committee of the Whole voted unanimously that day to advance it. As of a Sept 17, 2026 report, the Committee of the Whole had again voted unanimously (Sept 15, 2026) to send the ordinance to the full Council for a vote, but the full Council had not yet taken a final vote as of 2026-09-23 (paywalled article prevented confirming an exact scheduled date, but no evidence of adoption was found). Would be Dover's, and possibly Delaware's, first temporary ban on data center projects if passed; would not apply to New Castle/Kent County unincorporated-area rules already adopted separately.
